clue.text: Polish model, downright tense

definitions.meaning: to polish something is to refine it until it has no flaws
a model pupil is an ideal, flawless one
downright means utter, complete, as in a total stranger
a grammatical tense such as 'I have done', expressing completed action

explanation.surface: A Polish fashion model described as thoroughly tense.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row: 'Polish' is not the nationality but the verb, and each of the four words means the answer on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word is a synonym in its own sense: refine as a verb, ideal, utter, and the grammatical tense of completed action.

clue.text: Called with afterthought about accidents

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the afterthought wraps round the word for called

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
rang means called on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone phoned about accidents, adding a thought afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for minor crashes, especially car bumps; a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Water is assumed to be ingredient in fruit cake?

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or take in, so the water takes the little word inside it

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A baker's question: is water supposed to go into fruit cake?
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are one example of what goes into a fruit cake, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Try to convert Senegal? I've failed

indicators.note: failed suggests something broken down and fallen apart, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A missionary confesses that trying to convert Senegal was a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach the gospel to win followers is to attempt conversion; a synonym for proselytise.

clue.text: March is bad time, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: poor means of low quality, bad

explanation.surface: On reflection, March is a bad time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To move along in a body, as soldiers parade in file, is a synonym for marching.

clue.text: Crowning the young Diana R.?

definitions.meaning: a crowning achievement is the highest, ultimate one
Diana Ross began her career as lead singer of the Motown group the ..., so in her youth she was one member of it

explanation.surface: A question about crowning a youthful Diana, as if royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diana R.' tempts towards Princess Diana and a coronation, but it is Diana Ross of the Motown girl group.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest or ultimate is a synonym; and a single member of the Supremes group is one of them, singular.

clue.text: Mocking idiotic racialist

indicators.note: idiotic means foolish and confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ridiculing a stupid bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire ridicules its targets, so a derisive, sardonic tone is a synonym.

clue.text: Feature of mum first to attract dad

parts.note: a pap is a nipple, a feature of a mother's body

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A mother's feature that first drew the father to her.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish or old-fashioned word for father, a synonym.

clue.text: Veil females head to toe, uniformity primarily secured by lash

indicators.note: the head letter goes down to the toe, moving the word's first letter to the end

parts.note: hens are female birds

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the next word

parts.note: a rod is used to beat, a lash

indicators.note: primarily means just the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A harsh regime veils women head to toe, enforcing uniformity by the lash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to toe' sends H of HENS to the end, ENSH; U goes into ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap in a shroud is to cover completely, a synonym of veiling.

clue.text: Function central to each empty sports facility

indicators.note: central to means placed in the middle of what follows
empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Every empty sports centre performs some function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports facility' reads as one thing, but 'facility' alone is the definition, meaning ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility can mean ease of doing something, as in 'speaks French with facility'; a synonym.

clue.text: Self-help group cuddling cat and dog

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold in your arms, so the group's letters wrap around the cat

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is the best-known self-help group
a kit is a young cat, a kitten

explanation.surface: A support group hugging a cat and a dog, like therapy pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat and dog' reads as two animals, but the cat is wordplay and only 'dog' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of hound, an example of the category.

clue.text: Part of autumn operation employs army swimmers

parts.note: October, abbreviated Oct, is one month of autumn
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Part of an autumn military operation uses army swimmers, frogmen perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' is a pun on 'armed': eight-armed sea creatures are the swimmers, not soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: These eight-limbed sea creatures are humorously 'army' because each has so many arms; a playful description.

clue.text: Seeing red blood around home, gasp fearfully

indicators.note: around says the word for blood is placed round the word for home

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
in means at home

indicators.note: done fearfully, the letters are thrown into disorder and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees red at bloodshed near the house and gasps in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing red' looks like part of the gory scene, but it is the definition; 'fearfully' gives GSPA, a rearrangement of GASP.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom for becoming furious or frantic, equivalent to flying into a rage.

clue.text: Health food bargains offered regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A health food sold off cheaply on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal husk is a high-fibre staple, an example of food eaten for health.

clue.text: Prevent gains being split by nucleus of money launderers

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage

indicators.note: split by means the next piece breaks into the word

parts.note: gets means obtains, gains

indicators.note: a nucleus is the centre, so the middle letter is taken

explanation.surface: Stopping gains from being split by the core of a money-laundering gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money launderers' looks like criminals, but 'launderers' alone means cleaning agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powders and liquids are what launder clothes, so a playful agent-noun synonym.

clue.text: Born with limp, Eastern European's heard these offer complete freedom?

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
lank hair is limp and lifeless

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud and spelt as another word sounding the same

parts.note: a Czech is from the Czech Republic; with the 's this is said as Czechs

explanation.surface: A limp-from-birth Eastern European apparently enjoys complete freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Signed payment slips with the amount left empty give the holder freedom to fill in any sum: an idiom for carte blanche.

clue.text: Manspreading, perhaps, blighting men's igloo?

indicators.note: blighting means ruining, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Men sitting with legs splayed spoil the igloo for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Manspreading is a recently coined word, an example of a new term entering the language.

clue.text: Slavery in the real Spain twice dismissed by Catholic dignitary

indicators.note: by means next to, so the dignitary follows
dismissed means sent away, so those letters are removed
twice means the letter for Spain is taken two times over

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
Dom is a title given to certain Benedictine monks

explanation.surface: Slavery in the real Spain was twice abolished by a Catholic cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage or servitude to a master is a synonym for slavery.

clue.text: Scoff when rambling confession of perjurer retracted in Texas

indicators.note: in places the reversed confession inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: TX is the postal abbreviation for Texas

indicators.note: a statement retracted is taken back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a perjurer confessing would say I'm liar

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs while a perjurer retracts a rambling confession in a Texas court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' is food, not mockery; 'rambling' is hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack of nuts and dried fruit eaten by hikers is food (scoff) on a ramble.

clue.text: Edge along road, closely pursued by bear

indicators.note: something pursued has its follower behind it, so the second word comes after

parts.note: hard by means close by
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: A wilderness scene: someone on the roadside chased closely by a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is the verb, not the animal; 'hard' means close, as in 'hard by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The motorway verge strip for emergency stops is literally the paved edge running along a British road.

clue.text: M-m-member for T-t-t-tatton, personification of greed

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the stuttered Ms stand in for the stuttered Ts

parts.note: Tatton is a parliamentary seat in Cheshire, its three Ts echoed by the stutter
the stutter gives three Ms, M being the first letter of member, each standing in for one T of the seat's name

explanation.surface: A stammered jibe at the MP for Tatton, painted as the very embodiment of greed.
explanation.walkthrough: Each T of Tatton is swapped for an M; Tatton, a Cheshire seat, was then held by Chancellor George Osborne, adding the barb.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible wealth worshipped as a false god bears this name, so it embodies avarice.

clue.text: Unspoilt daughter and niece flourished

indicators.note: flourished, like a waved flag, signals the letters are swung into a new order

explanation.surface: A daughter and niece have grown up unspoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the Garden of Paradise in Genesis, so pristine and innocent: a synonym for untouched.

clue.text: Dry, cold deserts stinging nose

indicators.note: to desert is to leave, so the letter for cold leaves the word

parts.note: an acrid smell is sharp and stings the nose
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Dry cold air in deserts makes the nose sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' is a verb here, not sandy places.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land has little rainfall; a straight synonym for parched.

clue.text: They rescue you, reportedly trapped by retired bore on cruise

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the guard-like piece follows the word for cruise

parts.note: to coast is to cruise along without effort

indicators.note: trapped by means the next letter sits caught inside the reversed word
retired means drawn back, so the word for bore is read backwards

parts.note: a drag is something tedious, a bore

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is spoken, giving a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you is said like the letter U

explanation.surface: Rescuers save you from being stuck with a tiresome bore on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DRAG into GARD; 'reportedly' turns 'you' into U, held within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastal service saves people in danger at sea; the collective noun takes 'They'.

clue.text: Upset when admitting social worker is annual visitor

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the worker goes inside
upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading it upward

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
an ant is a social insect that works

explanation.surface: Someone upset when a social worker is admitted on a yearly visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is a colony insect, not a case worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas comes once a year on Christmas Eve, so he is a yearly caller.

clue.text: Ardent crowds removing clothes

indicators.note: clothes are the outer layer, so the word's outside letters are taken away

parts.note: swarms are crowds, as of insects or people

explanation.surface: Ardent crowds stripping off in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent and enthusiastic are both passionate, heated feelings; a synonym.

clue.text: Curses mother country

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone swears at their mother country.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation the word is an oath, so it stands for swearwords, uttered imprecations.

clue.text: English scorer scores, moving yard forward after Nasri's header

indicators.note: after puts the shifted word behind the initial letter
a header is the top, so the first letter of the footballer's name is used
moving signals a letter changing its place within the word
forward says the letter goes to the front of the word

parts.note: scores of things means many of them

explanation.surface: A football report: an English goal scorer pounces after Samir Nasri's header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' is a composer of film scores, not a goal getter. Michael Nyman scored The Piano; Nasri was a French footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Nyman is an English composer known for film soundtracks, so he writes scores.

clue.text: Most saying, "I can't think what to say"

parts.note: a maxim is a saying or proverb

parts.words: I can't think what to say
parts.note: um is the hesitation sound made when lost for words

explanation.surface: Someone saying they can't think what to say, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest possible amount is a synonym of the largest, as in 'the most you can get'.

clue.text: As nice as ever, First Lady ignored straying

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so these letters are rearranged
ignored means the name is left out of the word it sits inside

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman stays as pleasant as ever while the First Lady ignores her husband's straying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is the chemical symbol, not a link word; 'ignored' removes EVE from the fodder, leaving NICEASR for 'straying' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of this toxic element, atomic number 33, a crossword-favourite abbreviation.
